Synthetic catchment

Source: R/synthetic_catchment.R
synthetic_catchment.Rd

Builds a calibration problem with a known answer: synthetic rain and PET drive a PDM with chosen parameters, and its flow is corrupted the way a real gauge corrupts it. Calibrating to the result shows what a method can and cannot recover, since the truth is known.

Usage

synthetic_catchment(
  rain = NULL,
  truth = NULL,
  start = "2010-10-01",
  years = 10,
  dt = 24,
  method = "nsrp",
  area_km2 = 60,
  storms = NULL,
  error = list(sd = 0.05, memory_h = 72),
  highest_gauged_m3s = NULL,
  rating_bias = 0.15,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

rain

Forcing from synthetic_rain() or your own data frame; by default synthetic_rain(start, years, dt, method).

truth

The true configuration. By default, the standard preset (a lowland water balance: soil capacity up to 300 mm, slow recharge with kg 4000 h) with surface stores of 12 h each, and dt and area_km2 set. Under the default rain it evaporates about 310 mm a year, turns about 60 per cent of the rain into flow, and has a baseflow index near 0.6. Every calibrated parameter lies inside calibration_bounds(). Its dt must match the forcing's step.

start, years, dt, method

Passed to synthetic_rain() when rain is not given.

area_km2

Catchment area, km2, used when truth is not given.

storms

Optional data frame of added storms: time, depth_mm, duration_h.

error

List of sd (standard deviation of the log error) and memory_h (e-folding time of the error, hours). sd = 0 gives exact flow.

highest_gauged_m3s

Optional highest gauged flow, m3/s; flows above it carry the rating bias. Returned so it can be passed to register_data().

rating_bias

Fractional error of the recorded flow at twice the highest gauged flow.

seed

Optional seed for the rain and the error; the caller's random state is left untouched.

Value

A list, classed pdm_synthetic_catchment: forcing (time, rain, pet), observed (m3/s, as a gauge would record it), true_flow (m3/s), truth (configuration), highest_gauged_m3s, and notes, a list recording the rain method and parameters, the storms, the error and the rating bias.

Details

In order:

  1. Forcing. rain from synthetic_rain(), or a data frame you supply (with time, rain and pet).

  2. Storms. Each row of storms adds a storm: depth_mm spread over duration_h hours from time, in a symmetric triangular profile. Use them to guarantee floods larger than the generator would give in a short record.

  3. True flow. The truth configuration, started from a state spun up over the first year of forcing (three cycles), so the record starts in balance.

  4. Rating bias. With highest_gauged_m3s, flows above it are bent as an extrapolated rating would bend them: recorded = limit x (true / limit)^b, with b chosen so a flow twice the limit is recorded rating_bias low (15 per cent by default; negative values record high). Below the limit the rating is exact.

  5. Gauge error. A multiplicative error, persistent in time: in logs, an AR(1) process with standard deviation error$sd and an e-folding memory of error$memory_h hours.

The truth is the PDM itself, so the structure is exactly right, the rain exactly known and the error simpler than a real gauge's. Results on a synthetic catchment are a best case. Calibrate a different structure from truth to see what structural error does.

See also

synthetic_rain(), register_data(), calibrate_pdm()

Examples

river <- synthetic_catchment(years = 3, seed = 1,
  storms = data.frame(time = "2011-12-01", depth_mm = 120, duration_h = 48),
  highest_gauged_m3s = 20)
river
#> Synthetic catchment: 1095 steps of 24 h from 2010-10-01T00:00:00Z 
#>   Rain: nsrp - 798 mm a year; 1 added storm 
#>   True flow: mean 0.909 m3/s, peak 12.4 m3/s
#>   Gauge error: sd 0.05 in logs, memory 72 h
#>   Rating: exact to 20 m3/s, then 15 per cent low at twice that; 0 steps above
range(river$observed / river$true_flow)
#> [1] 0.8596667 1.1564223
